decisions.summary: A compact catalogue with a search-first header, scannable filters, and the existing STAR PYRAMIDS tour cards across all four trip categories.
constraints: Use only listed tours from the canonical tour data source
Keep current tour imagery, cards, detail links, blue and orange brand accents
Do not invent hotel amenities, live availability, reviews, or date-based booking data
Make filtering, sorting, pagination, mobile layout, and Arabic controls usable

decisions.summary: Image-led destination guides use a cinematic but bounded hero, an at-a-glance facts band, readable editorial sections, practical advice, and a contextual tour CTA.
constraints: Preserve STAR PYRAMIDS blue, orange, typography, header, and footer
Use truthful destination photography and practical travel content
Keep article text readable and responsive without oversized headings
Avoid nested cards and generic marketing-page composition

decisions.summary: Offer listings use one recognizable promotional card system across the homepage and full catalogue, supported by a sales-led hero, scannable inclusions, trust signals, and clear enquiry paths.
constraints: Never fabricate prices, countdowns, deadlines, availability, or inclusions
Use destination photography as the primary sales signal
Keep STAR PYRAMIDS blue and orange as purposeful conversion accents
Make the offer hierarchy, benefits, terms note, and next action clear on every viewport
Use the shared PromotionCard and render price or countdown UI only when verified data exists

decisions.summary: One-day tour pages share the multi-day package layout, image gallery, booking panel, facts, tabs, and section styling, with a shorter stop-by-stop visit plan instead of a day-by-day package itinerary.
constraints: Keep the visual structure aligned with the multi-day package detail page
Never imply unverified stops, times, inclusions, or cancellation terms
Use existing STAR PYRAMIDS blue, orange, photography, and typography
Use one responsive template for every one-day tour

decisions.summary: Every destination uses one image-led editorial template with destination-specific facts, signature experiences, a suggested rhythm, practical guidance, related tours, and a planning CTA.
constraints: Keep every destination data-driven through the shared Destination detail model
Use photography that clearly represents the destination or travel experience
Pull related tours from the existing catalogue instead of duplicating tour data
Keep advice practical, concise, responsive, and free of unverified prices or availability claims

decisions.summary: The contact route uses an image-led Egypt hero, clear local trust signals, a focused trip-enquiry form, transparent demo contact methods, and a simple three-step response story.
constraints: Keep phone and WhatsApp interactions explicitly local demo experiences until real contact details are approved
Use the existing STAR PYRAMIDS blue, orange, typography, photography, header, and footer
Keep the enquiry form honest about its preview-only behavior and do not imply server submission
Support English, Arabic RTL, keyboard navigation, reduced motion, and mobile layouts

decisions.summary: Login and registration share an image-led account shell with clear identity fields, complete country and calling-code selection, bilingual layouts, and honest previews for backend-dependent authentication.
constraints: Keep OAuth and account submission visibly in preview mode until a real backend integration is configured
Treat full name and username as separate account fields
Synchronize the selected country with the displayed mobile calling code
Preserve keyboard access, password visibility controls, validation, Arabic RTL, and responsive layouts

decisions.summary: Tour detail pages use an auto-advancing vertical social-reels slider for dashboard-managed video links, ordered newest first, followed by an auto-advancing slider of real related tour records.
constraints: Keep the primary tour image gallery unchanged and use video only in the journey media section
Support YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Vimeo, secure direct video URLs, and a safe external-link fallback
Never inject dashboard HTML or pass arbitrary URLs into an iframe
Auto-advance the rail only; never autoplay embedded media or its audio
Keep the 9:16 rail usable with touch, keyboard focus, English, Arabic RTL, and mobile layouts

decisions.direction: Stable Primary Header + Compact Sticky Navigation
decisions.summary: The full desktop header keeps its established navigation, while the scroll header reduces the menu to Home, Egypt Tours, Rent Car, Events, and one About company dropdown.
constraints: Do not change the desktop navigation shown before scrolling
Group About Us, Contact Us, and Blogs only inside the sticky About company dropdown
Keep the Egypt Tours dropdown available in both desktop header states
On mobile show only the menu button, logo, language control, and notification control in the top row
Hide the separate sticky header on mobile and retain an accessible mobile navigation drawer

decisions.summary: The events catalogue opens with a full-width photographic hero driven by the next real event, followed by its date, location, useful catalogue counts, and direct paths into the calendar.
constraints: Use the canonical events collection for the hero image, featured event, dates, locations, and counts
Keep the hero photographic and aligned with STAR PYRAMIDS blue and orange accents
Do not use abstract gradients, decorative circles, or invented availability claims
Keep the event cards visible immediately after the hero on desktop and mobile

decisions.summary: One-day tours, multi-day journeys, Nile cruises, and shore excursions share the selected Events hero proportions and image-led hierarchy while retaining their existing catalogue structures.
constraints: Use real tour images, featured records, locations, durations, and counts from the canonical tour data
Keep the selected Events hero height, overlay, typography, action hierarchy, rail, and responsive behavior consistent across all four categories
Preserve each page's filters, region navigation, cruise-type cards, tour cards, routes, and pagination
Support English, Arabic RTL, keyboard navigation, and mobile without inventing availability or operational claims

decisions.summary: Rent Car, Contact, About, Blogs, and Special Offers use the selected Events hero proportions and hierarchy, with page-specific featured content, metadata, calls to action, and truthful catalogue counts.
constraints: Share one PageShowcaseHero implementation instead of duplicating page-specific hero markup
Use existing project photography and canonical page data for featured records and statistics
Preserve every page's existing sections, forms, cards, interactions, and routes below the hero
Keep the hero responsive and bilingual with Arabic RTL support and no invented operational claims

decisions.summary: The blogs index uses a magazine-style featured guide followed by an aligned three-column journal grid, giving every recent story equal visual weight instead of generic catalogue cards.
constraints: Use canonical blog images, categories, dates, excerpts, and reading times
Keep blog cards visually distinct from tour, event, and offer cards
Preserve direct article links, keyboard focus, responsive layouts, and Arabic RTL behavior
Do not invent authors, popularity, comments, or editorial metadata

decisions.summary: Every event detail route uses its own visual identity, introduction, highlights, itinerary, inclusions, optional extras, location, and enquiry path inside one shared event-planning template.
constraints: Drive the hero and all detail sections from the canonical event record
Do not present a city as a confirmed venue or invent ticket availability, prices, or operational details
Keep the booking interaction an honest no-payment enquiry until backend confirmation exists
Support keyboard access, responsive layouts, English, and Arabic RTL

decisions.summary: A standalone customer dashboard connects bookings, the trip cart, saved tours, payments, a unified support conversation, profile details, and account settings through one bilingual backend-ready workspace with its own sidebar and topbar.
constraints: Use the existing browser-side cart, checkout bookings, enquiries, and canonical tour data until backend APIs replace the repository functions
Keep payment, receipt, and social login states honest and clearly backend-dependent
Use STAR PYRAMIDS navy, blue, and orange in a quiet operational layout instead of a marketing dashboard
Never render the public website header, promotion strip, footer, or floating support widgets inside account routes
Provide dashboard-native access to website return, trip search, language, currency, cart, notifications, profile, and sign out
Support English, Arabic RTL, keyboard access, reduced motion, and a mobile sidebar drawer
Keep Profile focused on identity and contact details, with Settings as a separate route for preferences, notifications, security, and privacy
Use the same first name, last name, username, email, complete country list, calling code, and national phone fields across registration, customer profile, and admin customer forms
Keep stable routes for overview, bookings, saved trips, payments, messages, profile, and settings
